title: Glass Dawn
warm:
Glass dawn meant [player_name] stood at Crownspire glass with Nolan Greer while morning threw city light as accusation and the choice narrowed to leave or stay—soft alibi deciding whether twelve steps across the hall would keep her or release her. Early thirties, she/her, neighbor-mistress—Detective Imani Brooks's homicide interest rose without a settled body. Vivienne's four fates stayed open: willing leave, paid vanish, dead, staging. Leaving or staying did not force any of them.

"Not marriage," Nolan said, mid-forties finance and tech, brutal charm scraped honest, cufflinks quiet. "Truth. Soft. Leave free if soft costs too much of you. Stay for bittersweet glass if unfinished promise across the hall is still a life you can breathe. Neither invents Milan. Neither invents a corpse. Neither sole-locks Vivienne."

Marcus Pell's traveling language waited downstairs. Rhea Quinn's slate still thinned. Unused perfume still breathed from the master bath she should not know. Wind sheer against floor-to-ceiling glass. Elevator chime late and early at once. Soft still meant pliable evidence wearing dawn.

She catalogued the glass the way Brooks would: neighbor across the hall, calendar gaps shared, soft cover choosing exit or endurance. Layer 9 made every hush a draft. Hope and dread shared the hallway. Nolan's hand settled at her waist—protective, unfinished, a vow that was not a ring.

"Leave free respects the door you walk through," he murmured. "Bittersweet glass keeps unfinished promise and elevator chime. Neither settles her four fates. Both spend us into endings that leave L10 doors open."

Black car at the curb. Wine rings on marble. [player_name] felt glass dawn fitting her mouth like expensive silk and understood that leaving Crownspire or staying would change which soft she could still claim—without forcing Vivienne into any single destiny.
